x: Commentary on Surah "al-Munāfiqūn" (The Hypocrites). In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Commentary on the saying of Him, Mighty be His mention:
h

When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God. And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars (1)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him:
h
When the hypocrites come to you
, O Muḥammad,
h
they say
with their tongues:
h
We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God. And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger
. Whether the hypocrites said that or not,
h
God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars

. He says: God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars in their reporting about themselves that they bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, for they do not believe that in their hearts and do not have faith in it, so they are liars in their report about their hearts in this. One of the scholars of Arabic used to say
n
regarding His saying
h
God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars

: He called their inner conviction a lie only because they concealed hypocrisy; just as He did not accept their faith though they displayed it, so He made them liars, because they concealed other than what they displayed.
Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h
They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they barred others from the path of God. Evil indeed is what they used to do (2)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: The hypocrites took their oaths as a shield — that is, their swearing.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: They have taken their oaths as a shield
. That is: their swearing as a shield.

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding the saying of God:
They have taken their oaths as a shield
. He said: They shield themselves with them. He said: That is because they believed, then disbelieved

c: It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
They have taken their oaths as a shield
. He says: their swearing by God that they are indeed of you, as a shield

x: His saying:
h
a shield

. That is: a covering with which they cover themselves, as the one who takes shelter shelters behind his shield in war and battle, and with it they protect themselves, their offspring and their wealth, and ward off harm from them.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: : that they might safeguard with it their blood and their wealth

x: His saying:
h
and so they barred others from the path of God
. He says: so they turned away from the religion of God with which He sent His Prophet, peace be upon him, and from His law that He legislated for His creation.
h
Evil indeed is what they used to do
. He says: Evil indeed is what these hypocrites, who took their oaths as a shield, used to do [in this world]
n
in taking their oaths as a shield, because of their lying and hypocrisy and the rest of their conduct.
Commentary on His saying:
h
That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and so they do not understand (3)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: What these hypocrites who took their oaths as a shield used to do was evil
n
only because they affirmed God and His Messenger, then disbelieved through their doubt about that and their denial of it.
His saying:
h
so their hearts were sealed

. He says: so God placed upon their hearts a seal of disbelief, shutting out faith. We have explained elsewhere than this place the nature of the sealing of the heart, with its evidences and the statements of the people of knowledge, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here
n
His saying:
h
and so they do not understand
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: So they cannot discern right from wrong, or truth from falsehood, because of God's sealing of their hearts.

c: Qatādah used to say about this what Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and so they do not understand
: They professed "there is no god but God and Muḥammad is the Messenger of God," peace be upon him, while their hearts denied it and refused it.

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h

And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are like propped-up timbers. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God destroy them; how are they deluded (4)

. The One whose mention is majestic says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him: And when you see these hypocrites, O Muḥammad, their bodies please you, because of the evenness of their build and the beauty of their forms,
h
and if they speak, you listen to their speech
. The One whose praise is majestic says: and if they talk, you hear their speech, their way of speaking resembling the speech of people,
h
They are like propped-up timbers
. He says: as if these hypocrites were propped-up timbers, with no good in them, no understanding and no knowledge; they are merely forms without minds, and figures
n
without intellects.
His saying:
h
They think every cry is against them
. The One whose praise is majestic says: These hypocrites, because of their wickedness
n

, their ill opinion and their weak certainty, think every cry is against them, for they are in dread that God will send down concerning them something that tears away their veils and exposes them, and makes it lawful for the believers to kill them, take their children captive and seize their wealth. So out of their fear of that, whenever a revelation from God comes down to His Messenger, they think it has come down for their destruction and ruin. God, majestic be His praise, says to His Prophet, peace be upon him: They are the enemy, O Muḥammad, so beware of them, for their tongues are with you when they meet you, while their hearts are against you, with your enemies; so they are an eye for your enemies against you.
His saying:
h
May God destroy them; how are they deluded
. He says: God disgrace them; to what direction are they turned away from the truth.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and I heard him say regarding the saying of God:
And when you see them, their bodies please you
— the verse. He said: These are the hypocrites. The reciters differed in the reading of His saying:
. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kūfah, except al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī, read
with a ḍammah on the khāʾ and the shīn

. It is as if they took it as a plural of a plural: they formed the plural of khashabah as khishāb, then pluralized khishāb as khushub, just as thamarah was pluralized as thimār, then thumur. It is also possible that khushub, with a ḍammah on the khāʾ and the shīn, is a plural of khashabah, in which the shīn is sometimes given a ḍammah and sometimes a sukūn, as they pluralized akamah as ukumun and ukmun, with a ḍammah on the alif and the kāf sometimes and a sukūn on the kāf sometimes, and as one says budn and budun, with a ḍammah on the dāl and with a sukūn, as plurals of badanah. Al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read it "khushbun" with a ḍammah on the khāʾ and a sukūn on the shīn

. The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings and two eloquent dialects, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is right. The sukūn on the middle letter in what comes as a plural of the pattern faʿalah on the pattern fuʿl, in nouns, is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as in their pluralizing badanah as budn and ajamah as ujm.

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h
And when it is said to them: Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you, they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant (5)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: And when it is said to these hypocrites: Come to the Messenger of God, he will ask forgiveness for you,
h
they turn their heads aside
. He says: they move and shake them, in mockery of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and of his asking forgiveness. The reciters read
h
lawwaw

with a doubled wāw, in the sense of reporting about them that they repeated the shaking and moving of their heads and did it often, except Nāfiʿ, who read it with the wāw lightened: "lawaw", in the sense that they did it once
n
. The correct view on this is the reading of those who doubled the wāw, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: The reciters read {lawwaw} with a doubled wāw, in the sense of reporting about them that they repeated the shaking and moving of their heads and did it often, except Nāfiʿ, who read it with the wāw lightened: "lawaw", in the sense that they did it once (2).
The correct view on this is the reading of those who doubled the wāw, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: His saying:
h
and you see them turning away while they are arrogant
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: and you see them turning their faces away from what they were called to,
h
while they are arrogant

. He says: and they are arrogant about going to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, that he might ask forgiveness for them. According to what has been reported, all of these verses concern ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl. That is because he said to his companions: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. And he said: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. Zayd ibn Arqam heard that and informed the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, about it. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, summoned him and asked him about what had been reported about him, and he swore that he had not said it. It was said to him: If only you would go to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and ask him to ask forgiveness for you.

So he began to turn his head aside and move it in mockery, meaning by that that he would not do what they suggested to him. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about him this surah from its beginning to its end.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said, and reports came to that effect.
Mention of the narration that came to that effect:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam told us, he said: Isrāʾīl told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Zayd ibn Arqam, he said:
m: I went out with my uncle

on a campaign, and I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl say to his companions: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse; if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. He said: I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him.

c: He sent for me and I told him,
m: and he sent to ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Ubayy] ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, and his companions, and they swore that they had not said it. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, called me a liar and believed him. A grief struck me such as had never struck me before, and I entered the house. My uncle said to me: What did you want, except
that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, would call you a liar and loathe you? He said: until God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
When the hypocrites come to you
. He said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, sent for me, and recited it, then said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, has confirmed you, O Zayd"
b.via: He sent for me and I

c: Abū Kurayb and al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Maʿrūf told us, both said:
m: Bukayr told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, he said: al-Ḥakam informed me, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī say: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam say: When ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said what he said — Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God — and said: If we return to Medina. He said: I heard him, so I went to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and mentioned it, and some of the Anṣār blamed me. He said: And he came and swore that he had not said that. So I returned to the house and slept. He said: Then the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, came to me, or word reached me — and I came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and he said: "God, Blessed and Exalted, has confirmed you and excused you." He said: And the verse was revealed:
They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God
b.via: Abū Kurayb and al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Maʿrūf

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Hāshim Abū al-Naḍr told us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, he said:
m: I heard Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī say: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam relate this hadith

c: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, from al-Ḥakam, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from Zayd ibn Arqam, he said:
m: We were with the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, on a campaign, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy said: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. He said: I went to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and told him, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy swore that nothing of the kind had happened. He said: My people blamed me and said: What did you want by this? He said: I went off and slept, grieved — or saddened. He said: Then the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, sent for me, or I came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and he said: "God has sent down your excuse and confirmed you." He said: And this verse was revealed:
They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it

m: Zayd ibn Arqam heard it and reported it to his guardian. He said: His guardian reported it to the Prophet, peace be upon him. He said: Then it was said to Zayd: Your ear has been vindicated.

m: it was said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy: O Abū Ḥubāb, severe verses have been revealed about you, so go to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, that he may ask forgiveness for you. He turned his head aside and said: You told me to believe, and I believed; you told me to give the zakāh of my wealth, and I gave it; there remains only that I prostrate to Muḥammad.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And when it is said to them: Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you, they turn aside
— the whole verse; he recited it until

: It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; that is because a boy of his relatives went to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and told him a report about him and a serious matter. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, summoned him, and he swore and denied it. The Anṣār turned on that boy and blamed and rebuked him. It was said to ʿAbd Allāh: If only you would go to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. He began to turn his head aside — that is: I will not do it — and said he had lied about him, so God revealed what you hear.

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,

, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; it was said to him: Come, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, will ask forgiveness for you. He turned his head aside and said: What did I say?
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said:

And when it is said to them: Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you

Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah: {And when it is said to them: Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you, they turn aside} — the whole verse; he recited it until {the defiantly disobedient}: It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; that is because a boy of his relatives went to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and told him a report about him and a serious matter.

x: Commentary on the saying of Him:
h
It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; God will never forgive them. Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people (6)

. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him: It is the same, O Muḥammad, for these hypocrites to whom it was said: Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you — whether you ask forgiveness for them for their sins,
h
or do not ask forgiveness for them, God will never forgive them
. He says: God will never pardon their sins, but will punish them for them.
h
Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people
. He says: God does not grant success in faith to the people who lie against it
n
, disbelieve in it and depart from obedience to Him.

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd also told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; God will never forgive them
. He said: This verse was revealed after the verse in Surah al-Tawbah:
If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will never forgive them
[al-Tawbah: 80]. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "[I will ask forgiveness for them]
more than seventy times." So God revealed:
It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; God will never forgive them

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h

They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand (7)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says:
h
They are the ones who say
. He means the hypocrites who say to their companions
n
h
Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God
, of his Emigrant companions,
h
until they disperse
. He says: until they scatter from around him.
His saying:
h
And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth
. He says: To God belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the keys to the treasuries of that; no one is able to give anyone anything except by His will,
h
but the hypocrites do not understand
that this is so; therefore they say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, until they disperse.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse
. He says: Do not feed Muḥammad and his companions until hunger strikes them and they leave their Prophet.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse
; he recited it to the end of the verse: This was the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy to his hypocrite companions: Do not spend on
Muḥammad and his companions until they abandon him, for if you were not spending on them, they would leave him and depart from him.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah:
m: They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse

m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:

They are the ones who say

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h
They say: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. But to God belongs all might, and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know (8)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: These hypocrites whose description He gave earlier say:
h
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker
from it; and by "the mightier" he means the stronger and more powerful. God, majestic be His praise, said:
h
But to God belongs all might
— that is, strength and power —
h
and to His Messenger and to the believers
in God,
h
but the hypocrites do not know
that. It is reported that the reason for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy's saying this was that a man of the Emigrants had struck
n
a man of the Anṣār.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad ibn Maʿmar told me, he said: Abū ʿĀmir told us, he said:
m: told us, from ʿAmr, he said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Anṣār were more numerous than the Emigrants; then the Emigrants became numerous. They went out on a campaign of theirs, and a man of the Emigrants struck a man of the Anṣār. He said: There was fighting between them until [the Anṣārī] cried out: O company of the Anṣār! and the Emigrant cried out: O company of the Emigrants! He said: That reached the Prophet, peace be upon him, and he said: "What is the matter with you, and the call of the days of ignorance?" They said: A man of the Emigrants struck a man of the Anṣār. He said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Leave it, for it is rotten." He said: Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. ʿUmar said: O Messenger of God, let me kill him. He said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Let people not say that the Messenger of God kills his companions"

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: They say: If we return to Medina
But to God belongs all might, and to His Messenger
. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl the Anṣārī, the chief of the hypocrites, said that, and some of the hypocrites with him.

c: Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī told me, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥakam told us, he said: My father told me, from ʿIkrimah,
m: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl had a son called Ḥubāb, whom the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, named ʿAbd Allāh. He said: O Messenger of God, my father harms God and His Messenger, so let me kill him. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to him: "Do not kill your father." Then he came to him again and said: O Messenger of God, [my father harms God and His Messenger, so let me kill him. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to him: "Do not kill your father." He said: O Messenger of God,]

perform ablution so that I may give him to drink from your ablution water; perhaps his heart will soften. So the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, performed ablution and gave it to him, and he went with it to his father and gave it to him to drink, then said to him: Do you know what I gave you to drink? His father said to him: Yes, you gave me your mother's urine to drink. His son said to him: No, by God, rather I gave you to drink the ablution water of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. ʿIkrimah said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was a man of great standing among them. And concerning them this verse was revealed, about the hypocrites:
They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse
. And he is the one who said:
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it

. He said: When they reached Medina — the city of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and those with him — his son took the sword, then said to his father: You claim: If we return to Medina, the mightier will drive out the weaker from it; by God, you will not enter it until the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, permits you

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
m: that a man of the Emigrants struck a man of the Anṣār with his foot, and that is serious among the people of Yemen, so he called out: O Emigrants! O Anṣār! He said: The Emigrants were more numerous than the Anṣār that day. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Leave it, for it is rotten." Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said:
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it

c: ʿImrān ibn Bakkār al-Kalāʿī told me, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told us, he said: Abū Isḥāq told us that Zayd ibn Arqam informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said:
m: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. And he said: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. He said: Zayd told me that he informed the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, of the words of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy came and swore to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, that he had not said that. Abū Isḥāq said: Zayd said to me: I sat in my house until God sent down the confirmation of Zayd and the denial of ʿAbd Allāh in: "When the hypocrites come to you."
b.via: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it
; he recited the entire verse to:

. He said: A hypocrite of great hypocrisy said it, concerning two men who fought each other, one a Ghifārī and the other a Juhanī. The Ghifārī overcame the Juhanī, and there was an alliance between Juhaynah and the Anṣār, so a man among the hypocrites, namely Ibn Ubayy, said: O sons of al-Aws! O sons of al-Khazraj! Your companion and ally is at stake! Then he said: By God, the likeness of us and Muḥammad is only as the proverb says: Fatten your dog and it will eat you
. By God, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it.

x: Some of them carried it to the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, and ʿUmar said: O Prophet of God, order Muʿādh ibn Jabal to strike the neck of this hypocrite. He said: "Let people not say that Muḥammad kills his companions." It was mentioned to us that a man among the hypocrites was spoken of at length in his presence. He said: "Does he pray?" He said: Yes, but there is no good in his prayer. He said: "I have been forbidden to kill those who pray; I have been forbidden to kill those who pray."

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, he said:
m: Two men fought, one from Juhaynah and the other from Ghifār, and Juhaynah was an ally

of the Anṣār, and the Ghifārī overcame him. A man among them of great hypocrisy said: Your companion, your companion! By God, the likeness of us and Muḥammad is only as the proverb says: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. By God, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it — and they were on a journey. A man who had heard him came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and told him that. ʿUmar said: Order Muʿādh to strike off his neck. He said: "By God, let people not say that Muḥammad kills his companions." So there was revealed concerning them:
They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God

x: His saying:
h
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan,
m: that a boy came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God, I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy say such and such. He said: "Perhaps you were angry with him." He said: No, by God, O Prophet of God, I heard him say it. He said: "Perhaps your hearing erred?" He said: No, by God, O Prophet of God, I heard him say it. He said: "Perhaps it was made to seem so to you." He said: No, by God. He said: So God sent down a confirmation of the boy:
If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it
, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, took hold of the boy's ear and said: "Your ear has been vindicated, your ear has been vindicated, boy"

c: Yūnus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of God:
the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it
. He said: The hypocrites used to call the Emigrants "al-jalābīb." And he said: Ibn Ubayy said: I have put these jalābīb
under my command. He said: He said this between Amaj

; they had quarreled over water, and the Emigrants had prevailed over the water. He said: Ibn Ubayy also said: By God, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it; I told you: Do not spend on them; if you left them they would find nothing to eat, and they would leave and flee. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God, do you not hear what Ibn Ubayy is saying? He said: "What is that?" He told him, and said: Let me strike off his neck, O Messenger of God. He said: "Then many noses in Yathrib would quiver with rage over him." ʿUmar said: If you dislike, O Messenger of God, that a man of the Emigrants should kill him, then order Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, and they will kill him. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "I dislike that people should say that Muḥammad kills his companions. Call ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy for me." So he called him for him. He said: "Do you not see what your father is saying?" He said: What does he say, may my father and mother be your ransom? He said: "He says: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it." He said: He has spoken truly, by God, O Messenger of God: you, by God, are the mightier, and he is the weaker. By God, you came to Medina, O Messenger of God, and the people of Yathrib know that there is no one in it more dutiful than I, and if it would please God and His Messenger that I bring his head to them, I will bring it. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "No." When they came to Medina, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy stood at its gate with the sword against his father, then said: Are you the one who said: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it? By God, you will come to know whether might belongs to you or to the Messenger of God! By God, his shade will not shelter you, nor will you ever shelter in it, except with the permission of God and His Messenger. He said: O Khazraj, my son bars me from my house! O Khazraj, my son bars me from my house! He said: By God, you will never shelter in it except with his permission. Men gathered around him and spoke to him. He said: By God, he will not enter it except with the permission of God and His Messenger. They went to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and told him. He said: "Go to him and tell him: Let him be and his dwelling." They went to him. He said: Now that
the command of the Prophet, peace be upon him, has come, then yes.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salamah and ʿAlī ibn Mujāhid told us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah,
m: from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr, and from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān. He said: Each of them told me part of the story of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. They said: It reached the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, that Banū al-Muṣṭaliq were gathering against him, their leader being al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Ḍirār, the father of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith, the wife of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, heard of them, he went out to them until he met them at one of their wells called al-Murayṣīʿ, on the side of Qudayd toward the coast. The people drew up in ranks and fought, and God defeated Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and some of them were killed; and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, awarded as spoils their children, women and wealth, which God gave him as booty. A man of Banū Kalb ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿĀmir ibn Layth ibn Bakr, called Hishām ibn Ṣubābah, had been struck down by a man of the Anṣār from the clan of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, who thought he was one of the enemy and killed him by mistake. While the people
were at that well, the water-carriers came, and with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was a hired man of his from Banū Ghifār, called [Jahjāh ibn Saʿīd]
, who was leading his horse for him. Jahjāh

and Sinān al-Juhanī, an ally of Banū ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, crowded each other at the water and fought, and the Juhanī cried out: O company of the Anṣār! and Jahjāh (4) cried out: O company of the Emigrants! ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl became angry; he had with him a group of his people, among them Zayd ibn Arqam, a young boy. He said: Have they really done it? They have rivaled us and outnumbered us in our own land! By God, we and these jalābīb of Quraysh are only as the proverb says: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. By God, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said: This is what you have done to yourselves: you let them settle in your land and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you withheld from them what is in your hands, they would move to a land other than yours. Zayd ibn Arqam heard that, and went with it to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, which was when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, had finished with his enemy

, and told him the news. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was with him, and he said: O Messenger of God, order ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ibn Waqsh to kill him. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "How, ʿUmar, when people will say that Muḥammad kills his companions? No; rather, give the call to depart" — and that was at an hour at which the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, did not usually set out — so the people set out. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy had gone to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, when he learned that Zayd ibn Arqam had reported to him what he had heard from him, and he swore by God: I did not say what he said, nor did I speak it. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was a noble and great man among his people, and those of the Anṣār who were present with the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: O Messenger of God, perhaps the boy was mistaken in his report and did not retain what the man said, out of kindness
to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and in defense of him. When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, set off

and rode on, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of prophethood and gave him salām, then said: O Messenger of God, you have set out at an unusual hour, one at which you did not usually set out. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to him: "Has what your companion said not reached you?" He said: Which companion, O Messenger of God? He said: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy." He said: And what did he say? He said: "He claims that if he returns to Medina, the mightier will drive out the weaker from it." Usayd said: Then you, by God, O Messenger of God, will drive him out if you wish; he, by God, is the abased one, and you are the mighty one. Then he said: O Messenger of God, be gentle with him, for by God, God brought you when his people were stringing beads for him to crown him, and he thinks you have stripped him of a kingdom. Then the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, walked with the people all that day until evening, and that night until morning, and the early part of the next day until the sun troubled them. Then he made the people halt, and they had scarcely felt the touch of the ground
They say: If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it. But to God belongs all might, and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know (8)

when they fell asleep. He only did that to occupy the people from the talk that had occurred the day before, the talk of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy. Then he set out with the people and took the route of the Ḥijāz until he halted at a water in the Ḥijāz above al-Naqīʿ

. When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, set out, a violent wind blew upon the people that troubled them and they were afraid of it, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Do not fear, for it blew only because of the death of a great one of the great ones of the disbelievers." When they reached Medina, they found that Rifāʿah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tābūt, of Banū Qaynuqāʿ, who was one of the great ones of the Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites, had died that day. The surah was revealed in which God mentioned the hypocrites, regarding ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl and those with him of like conduct, and He said:
When the hypocrites come to you

. When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, took hold of Zayd's ear and said: "This is the one whose ear God has vindicated." And what his father had done reached ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq told me, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah,
m: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God, it has reached me that you wish to kill ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy for what has reached you about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it, and I will bring you his head; for by God, the Khazraj know that there was no man among them
more dutiful to his father than I, and I fear that you will order someone else

to kill him, and my soul will not let me look at the killer of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy walking among the people without killing him, and so I would kill a believer for a disbeliever and enter the Fire. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Rather, we will [be gentle with him and treat well]

his companionship as long as he remains with us." After that day, whenever he committed an offense, it was his own people who reproached him, seized him, treated him harshly and threatened him. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, when that reached him about their conduct: "What do you think, ʿUmar? By God, had I killed him on the day you told me to kill him, noses would have quivered with rage over him; were I to order them today to kill him, they would kill him." He said: ʿUmar said: By God, I now know that the command of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, is greater in blessing than my command

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h
O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that, those are the losers (9)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger,
h
let not your wealth distract you

. He says: let not your wealth or your children cause you heedlessness of the remembrance of God. It is from "alhaytuhu ʿan kadhā wa-kadhā" (I distracted him from such and such): "fa-lahā huwa yalhū lahwan" (so he was distracted). From this is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays
n

: "And a woman like you, pregnant and nursing, I came to her by night … and distracted her from her amulet-wearing child of a year." It was also said: what is meant by the remembrance of God, majestic be His praise, in this place is the five prayers.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Sinān, from Thābit, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk:
m: O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of God

x: His saying:
h
And whoever does that
. He says: and whoever is distracted by his wealth and his children from the remembrance of God,
h
those are the losers
. He says: they are the ones cheated of their share of the honor of God and His mercy, Blessed and Exalted.
Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h

And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says: My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term, so I could give charity and be (2) among the righteous (10) But God will never delay a soul when its term has come; and God is Aware of what you do (11)

. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: And spend, O you who believe in God and His Messenger, of the wealth We have provided you, before death comes to one of you and he says, when death descends upon him: My Lord, why did You not delay me, granting me respite in my term to a short term,
h
so I could give charity
. He says: so I could purify my wealth (by zakāh),
h
and be (2) among the righteous
. He says: and act in obedience to You and fulfill Your obligations. It was also said: What is meant by His saying
h
and be (2) among the righteous
is: and perform pilgrimage to Your Sacred House.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yūnus and Saʿīd ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, Saʿīd said: Sufyān told us,
m: and Yūnus said: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Janāb, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: There is no one who dies without having paid the zakāh on his wealth and without having performed pilgrimage, except that he asks to return (to the world). They said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, you do not cease bringing us things we do not recognize. He said: I recite to you from the Book of God:
And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says: My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term, so I could give charity
. He said: I would pay the zakāh on my wealth,
. He said: I would perform pilgrimage

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Abū Sinān, from a man, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said:
m: What prevents any of you, if he has wealth on which zakāh is due, from paying the zakāh, and if he is able to perform the pilgrimage, from performing it, before death comes to him and he asks his Lord for a return and is not granted it? A man said: Do you not fear God? Does the believer ask for a return? He said: Yes; shall I recite to you Qur'an? So he recited:
O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of God
. The man said: What makes the pilgrimage obligatory for me? He said: A mount to carry him and provisions to bring him there

c: ʿAbbād ibn Yaʿqūb al-Asadī and Faḍālah ibn al-Faḍl told us; ʿAbbād said:
m: , the freedman of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, informed us. And Faḍālah said: Bazīʿ told us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim regarding His saying:
if only You would delay me for a short term, so I could give charity
. He said: so that I might give charity through the zakāh of my wealth,

c: It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:

to the end of the surah: It is the believing man to whom death comes while he has much wealth on which he did not pay zakāh, from which he did not perform pilgrimage, and from which he did not give the due of God; he asks for a return at death, so that he might purify his wealth. God said:
But God will never delay a soul when its term has come

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of God
and spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you

. He said: It is the believing man when death comes to him while he has wealth on which he did not pay zakāh, from which he did not perform pilgrimage, and from which he did not give the due of God; so he asks for a return at death in order to give charity from his wealth and pay zakāh. God said:
But God will never delay a soul when its term has come

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān:
m: so I could give charity and be (2) among the righteous
; he said: zakāh and pilgrimage. The reciters differed in the reading of His saying:
. The majority of the reciters of the major cities, except Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr, read
in the jussive, coordinating it with the sense of His saying
, since it has no fā' — for if His saying
had no fāʾ, it would be jussive. Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr read: "wa-akūna", with the wāw retained and the verb in the subjunctive, coordinating it with His saying
; they put "wa-akūna" in the subjunctive since
is subjunctive. The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is right.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of His saying: {and be among the righteous}.

The majority of the reciters of the major cities, except Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr, read {wa-akun} in the jussive, coordinating it with the sense of His saying {so I could give charity}, since it has no fā' — for if His saying {fa-aṣṣaddaqa} had no fāʾ, it would be jussive.

x: His saying:
h
But God will never delay a soul when its term has come
. He says: God will never postpone anyone's term, extending it for him, when his term arrives; rather, He cuts him off.
h
and God is Aware of what you do

. He says: God has full awareness and knowledge of the deeds of His servant, and encompasses all of them; nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for them — the doer of good for his good, and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. End of the commentary on Surah "al-Munāfiqūn".

notes.ar: ويروى "أسْمِن"، وأول من قاله حازم بن المنذر الحماني. تنظر قصة هذا المثل في مجمع الأمثال 2/ 106.

notes.en: "Jalābīb Quraysh" is a nickname for those of the Emigrants who had accepted Islam, which the polytheists gave them. The original meaning of jalābīb is coarse wrappers, the singular being jilbāb, which they used to wrap themselves in, so they nicknamed them with it. Sharḥ gharīb al-sīrah 3/40.
notes.ar: جلابيب قريش: هو لقب لمن كان أسلم من المهاجرين، لقَّبهم بذلك المشركون. وأصل الجلابيب الأُزُر الغلاظ، واحدها جلباب، وكانوا يلتحفون بها، فلقَّبوهم بذلك. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 40.

notes.en: Amaj: a town in the outskirts of Medina, now one of the towns of the Ḥijāz. See Jughrāfiyyat shibh jazīrat al-ʿArab by Kaḥḥālah p. 139.
notes.ar: أمج: بلد من أعراض المدينة وهي من بلدان الحجاز الآن. ينظر جغرافية شبه جزيرة العرب لكحالة ص 139.

notes.en: ʿUsfān: a village between Medina and Mecca. Ibid. pp. 30, 34, 170.
notes.ar: عسفان: قرية بين المدينة ومكة. السابق ص 30، 34، 170.

notes.en: Al-Kadīd: a place in the Ḥijāz. See Muʿjam al-buldān 4/245.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "حذارا"، والحدب: التحنن والعطف. شرح غريب السيرة 3/ 40.

notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "استقبل".

notes.en: Al-Naqīʿ: a place between Mecca and Medina. Muʿjam mā istaʿjam 4/1323.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T2, T3 and the source of the report: "Baqʿāʾ". Naqʿāʾ is a place behind Medina above al-Naqīʿ, in the territory of Muzaynah, on the route of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in the campaign of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. See Muʿjam al-buldān 4/805.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3، ومصدر التخريج: "بقعاء". ونقعاء موضع خلف المدينة فوق النقيع من ديار مزينة وكان طريق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة بني المصطلق. ينظر معجم البلدان 4/ 805.

notes.en: Sīrat Ibn Hishām 2/290–292.

notes.en: In T2, T3: "wa-akūna" ("and I will be"). This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Muḥayṣin, as will come shortly. See Ḥujjat al-qirāʾāt p. 710; in al-Sabʿah it is stated that the reading without the wāw is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī, and with the wāw the reading of the rest. See al-Sabʿah p. 637.
notes.ar: في ت 2، ت 3: "وأكون". وهي قراءة أبي عمرو وابن محيصن. كما سيأتي قريبًا. وينظر حجة القراءات ص 710، وفي السبعة أن القراءة بغير الواو هي قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي. وبالواو قراءة الباقين. ينظر السبعة ص 637.
